pages.name: Home

props.text: Kitchen sink — a guided tour of every toolback feature

Each page demonstrates one feature: what it does, where its scripts live, and tips for trying it. The menu below IS the pages & navigation demo — every button is one line of script: page.go('…'). Press Run (F3 or ⌥3) and click.

props.title: The tour
props.text: Everything here is one ordinary .toolback.json book built from the same palette controls. Open any object's Script panel while designing — scripted events are marked with a • in the event dropdown. While a run is active, the Store tab on the right shows every store.set live.
Tip: the ↶ ↷ buttons (or ⌘Z) undo any design edit — even grouping or deleting. Try it as you explore.

pages.name: Store

props.text: Store & dynamic labels — {{key}} makes state visible
store.set(key, value) stores a value; {{key}} in any Text property displays it and re-renders on every store.set. Press Run, type below, and watch the labels — plus the Store tab on the right.

Colours & fonts: set the Background / Text colour / Font fields in the Selection panel — 'red', 'navy', '#3b82f6', rgb(…) — or from scripts: try the green button (its click script runs self.background = 'green').

Where the scripts live: nameInput's Script panel has two handlers (input + change) reading event.target.value. clickButton has click + dblclick — a double-click fires click twice, then dblclick resets the count. Lock click writes clickButton.enabled.
The labels are NOT scripted: their Text property is just Hi {{who}} / Clicks: {{clicks}}. Unset keys render empty. Script-side, read values with store.get — typing {{ in a script offers exactly that.

pages.name: Self

props.text: self — the object that owns the script

self is a system property: the object the currently executing script belongs to. In a button's own script self is that button; in a group's script self is the GROUP (while target is the member that was clicked); in the page script self is the page. Like ToolBook's self, it cannot be set. this is an alias for self.
The three buttons below share the same Text binding — I am {{self.name}} — and no script touches their text:
Try it: select a button and press ⧉ (or ⌥D) — the duplicate lands +24px down-right and already shows its own name. The binding does the work; nothing to edit. Undo with ⌘Z.

Where the scripts live: each button's click script is one line — store.set('lastSelf', self.name). The name display is the Text property I am {{self.name}}, a binding rather than a script. {{this.name}} works too.

self vs target (ToolBook heritage): in a group script, self is the group itself and target is the member that was clicked — the Groups page shows the pair in action. In the page script, self.name is the page name.

pages.name: Groups

props.text: Groups & forward — the ToolBook event rule

Rule: the innermost script for an event runs and STOPS there unless it calls forward(). An object with no script for that event lets the event pass to its parent group automatically. In a group's script, target is the member that was clicked and self is the group itself.
groupA below holds two buttons AND another group (groupInner) holding a third — nested groups. Press Run and click each button:

Try it: click "I have a script + forward()" — its own script runs, then forward() continues up to groupA (groupRan reads self = groupA, target = btnFwd). Click "I have no script" or the nested button — no member script exists, so the event walks btnDeep → groupInner → groupA and the group handler catches it with target = the button you clicked.

Where the scripts live: exactly two. groupA's click handler (click the group once to select it — double-click drills in, Esc steps out) is store.set('groupRan', self.name + ' saw ' + target.name). btnFwd's click is store.set('memberRan', self.name) followed by forward(). groupInner and the other buttons have NO scripts — which is precisely why the message passes through them.
Design tip: ⌥G groups a selection, ⌥U ungroups, double-click drills one level per double-click, Esc steps out one level and is ignored at the outermost level.

pages.name: Motion

props.text: Scripted motion — x / y / width / height, await, pageEnter
Positions and sizes are writable from scripts. pageEnter already ran the drop-in animation on the mover card the moment this page opened.

props.title: I move
props.text: pageEnter drops me in from the top

Where the scripts live: the drop-in animation is pageEnter on this page (an async loop stepping mover.y with await). Random spot and Grow / shrink write mover.x/y/width/height directly. Reset box calls resetBox() — a shared page function, callable from any object script. pageLeave records the visit for the You-left label.

pages.name: Events

props.text: Each object can carry a script per event (the Script panel's event dropdown marks scripted ones with a •). A double-click fires click, click, then dblclick — browser rules.

Where the scripts live: all on the two objects. evDemo has click / dblclick / mouseenter / mouseleave (each writes '… on ' + self.name); typer has input / change. event is the raw DOM event, so event.target.value reads the field's live text.

Stop the run (F3) and try these on the group below. Undo/redo: ⌘Z / ⌘⇧Z or the ↶ ↷ buttons — every design edit is undoable, including grouping, duplicating and deleting. Duplicate: ⧉ or ⌥D copies the selection +24px down-right (a group copies its whole subtree, re-idded and re-named). Group/ungroup: ⌥G / ⌥U.

Copy JSON: the { } JSON button in the Selection panel copies the selected object — sub-objects included — as pretty-printed JSON (a multi-selection copies an array). Great for describing structures. Drill into groups: double-click descends one level per double-click; Esc steps out one level and is ignored at the outermost — it never deselects.

This pair arrives pre-grouped: click once selects the group, double-click drills in, Esc steps out. With the group selected press ⧉ — the whole subtree duplicates with fresh names. ⌥U ungroups; ⌘Z undoes any of it.

Also in the editor: Des/Tab/Mob previews breakpoints (objects without their own rect fall back to desktop); drag the splitter to widen the properties panel; the Objects tab is a tree with group members indented; the Store tab streams store.set calls during a run.

pages.name: Npm

props.text: npm libraries — any package, one import line

Any npm package works in scripts. The three buttons below all start from the same script-built two-note song (C4 → E4): Build re-parses it (data path), Play makes it audible through Tone.js (audio path — browsers demand a gesture first, and a click is one), and Download saves it as a real .mid file (file path). Package docs say import { Midi } from '@tonejs/midi' — in toolback the same line goes inside a function, awaited.

Where the scripts live: three async page functions. parseDemo (data) uses @tonejs/midi only; playDemo (audio) does await import('tone'), Tone.start() to unlock the AudioContext, then a PolySynth schedules track.notes at note.time + Tone.now(); downloadDemo (file) wraps midi.toArray() in a Blob and clicks a temporary <a download>. buildMidi() builds the song once and all three share it. Repeat imports are cheap — modules are cached. 'tone' isn't on the shelf yet, so previews fetch it from esm.sh; add it with pnpm --filter @toolback/libs add tone to embed it offline.

pages.name: Viewers

props.text: Markdown & HTML viewers — rich content from a prop

Two read-only viewer controls. The markdown viewer renders its Text property from Markdown; the HTML viewer injects its html property as raw markup. Both accept {{key}} bindings inside the source and re-render on every store.set. Press Run (F3) and hit +1 score.

## Score: {{demoScore}}

Markdown is written in the **Text** property and rendered live.

- the heading updates on every `store.set`
- lists, **bold**, `code`, quotes, tables…

> Both viewers are ordinary objects — move, resize and script them.

props.html:
Raw HTML

This markup comes from the html property.

  • Any tags work
  • Authors are trusted — no sanitiser

props.text: Where it lives: vwMd's Text property is "## Score: {{demoScore}}" — {{key}} resolves in the source before the Markdown renders, so the heading tracks the store. vwHtml's html property is injected as-is (raw HTML, no sanitiser — books already run your own scripts).

pages.name: Canvas

props.text: Each canvas runs its draw script in the Script tab. Static art repaints on every store.set; the wave and orbit call self.animate() for a per-frame loop that stops automatically on page change.
Static scene — recolour the sun with the button

on.draw:
const ctx = self.ctx
const w = self.width, h = self.height
const sky = ctx.createLinearGradient(0, 0, 0, h)
sky.addColorStop(0, '#0ea5e9')
sky.addColorStop(0.6, '#fde68a')
sky.addColorStop(1, '#fb923c')
ctx.fillStyle = sky
ctx.fillRect(0, 0, w, h)
ctx.beginPath()
ctx.arc(w * 0.72, h * 0.42, Math.min(w, h) * 0.16, 0, Math.PI * 2)
ctx.fillStyle = store.get('sunColor') || '#fff7ed'
ctx.fill()
ctx.beginPath()
ctx.moveTo(0, h)
ctx.quadraticCurveTo(w * 0.25, h * 0.55, w * 0.5, h * 0.78)
ctx.quadraticCurveTo(w * 0.75, h * 0.98, w, h * 0.7)
ctx.lineTo(w, h)
ctx.closePath()
ctx.fillStyle = '#166534'
ctx.fill()
ctx.beginPath()
ctx.moveTo(0, h)
ctx.quadraticCurveTo(w * 0.4, h * 0.78, w * 0.85, h)
ctx.closePath()
ctx.fillStyle = '#14532d'
ctx.fill()

const ctx = self.ctx
const w = self.width, h = self.height
const t = performance.now() / 1000
ctx.fillStyle = '#111827'
ctx.fillRect(0, 0, w, h)
const cx = w / 2, cy = h / 2
for (let i = 0; i < 12; i++) {
  const a = t + (i * Math.PI * 2) / 12
  const r = Math.min(w, h) * (0.18 + 0.12 * Math.sin(t * 1.5 + i))
  ctx.beginPath()
  ctx.arc(cx + Math.cos(a) * r, cy + Math.sin(a) * r, 7, 0, Math.PI * 2)
  ctx.fillStyle = 'hsl(' + (i / 12) * 360 + t * 40 + ', 80%, 60%)'
  ctx.fill()
}
ctx.save()
ctx.translate(cx, cy)
ctx.rotate(t)
ctx.beginPath()
for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) {
  const a = (i * Math.PI * 2) / 5
  const x = Math.cos(a) * Math.min(w, h) * 0.42
  const y = Math.sin(a) * Math.min(w, h) * 0.42
  if (i === 0) ctx.moveTo(x, y)
  else ctx.lineTo(x, y)
}
ctx.closePath()
ctx.lineWidth = 3
ctx.strokeStyle = '#f59e0b'
ctx.stroke()
ctx.restore()

on.click:
store.set('spin', !store.get('spin'))
const on = store.get('spin')
cvWave.animate(on)
cvOrbit.animate(on)

props.text: Tip: open a canvas and switch the event dropdown to draw. self.ctx is the standard 2D context; self.width/self.height are the object's size in CSS pixels, and the runtime keeps the backing store crisp on every preview width.
